sentences.text: The genus Baharijodon is known from a single tooth that was first illustrated by Ernst Stromer in 1933 and formally named by Oskar Kuhn in 1936.
Taxonomically, Baharijodon belongs to the parent group Crocodylia and is classified within the class Reptilia.
Fossils of this animal come from the Bahariya Formation in Egypt, dating to the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
In 1979, Éric Buffetaut and P. Taquet reclassified the tooth as belonging to the family Trematochampsidae, a change that remains a point of discussion regarding its precise evolutionary placement.
